newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Trade seen sailing in narrow strait.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Trade seen sailing in narrow strait.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to range trade this week as a Europe-bound ship was due to finish soon loading fresh supplies from the Philippines, vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
MV Luctor is expected to leave the Philippines this week after loading 35,000 tonnes of coconut oil, they said.
Another ship, MV Blue Sapphire, was also expected to arrive in the Philippines on June 6.
"We are in a lull... waiting for news on Sapphire and effects of the rains in southern Philippines," a senior trader told Reuters. "Prices will likely move in a narrow band of $5 up or down."
Coconut oil sellers quoted $642.50 per tonne CIF on Saturday against $630 for buyers, trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines said.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam dropped to 15,972 tonnes as of May 23 from the previous week's 19,475.
Talk of a possible delay of a major shipment of Philippine coconut oil for June and July pushed up prices by $20 per tonne since May 19 before it stabilised last Thursday on news of Luctor's arrival.
Sapphire was supposed to load 35,000 tonnes of Philippine coconut oil in May but was stuck in China, traders said.
"Logistics problems due to ship delays and weather conditions such as typhoons in the Philippines will determine price swings in the second half of the year," a trader said.
The Philippines is the world's largest exporter of coconut products.
Traders said domestic prices of copra and coconut oil were up slightly on Monday due a slowdown of copra arrivals to the mills.
Copra buyers quoted 9.20 pesos a kg on Monday from last week's nine while buyers quoted coconut oil at 16.50 pesos per kg from the previous 16.20.
Traders said rains in coconut growing areas in southern Philippine in the past several days slowed transport of copra to the mills.
Rainy season in the Philippines start in May and last up to November.
